# Knowledge-Core: Workflows

Work only on the existing `dev` branch. Generate with repository scripts or `make generate`; after Go module changes run `make tidy`.

Every change must pass `make ci`. Go concurrency or lifecycle changes also run `make race`. Node fixture changes under `services/collaboration/interop` run `npm ci` then `npm run ci`. IDL changes additionally run `go run ./scripts/idlguard compat-git <merge-base> idl`.

Command maps remain in the generated workflows appendix.

<!-- fact:workflows.development status:verified sources:user-confirmed, user-confirmed-schema-v2-rerecord -->

Pushes to `dev` trigger the reusable Python CI control image from ci-templates. All trusted release jobs use the organization self-hosted runner labels `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`, and `devops`; system Docker cleanup is limited to the dedicated Buildx cache and runner state. Control-image containers run as the current runner UID and GID (`docker run --user $(id -u):$(id -g)` with a writable HOME); Docker config is mounted at `/ci/docker` rather than `/root/.docker`; runner cache is `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/../../_cache/knowledge-core` and Go tools use `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE`. The host runner uses systemd `HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:10991` (sing-box HTTP inbound) with `NO_PROXY` for Harbor, cluster, and npmmirror, and `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` so Node 24 actions including `create-github-app-token` post honor that proxy; `ci_run` forwards those variables into the control image. Build and compile parallelism defaults to 75% of effective runner CPUs (affinity and cgroup quota), configurable with `BUILD_CPU_PERCENT`; `BUILD_JOBS` is only a bounded emergency override. The pipeline runs `make ci` and Collaboration Node interop checks on Node 24.18.1 from npmmirror, without GitHub Actions npm cache restore; `npm audit` uses `https://registry.npmjs.org` because npmmirror does not implement the security advisories API; detects affected services; warms pinned base images into Harbor; builds affected images using only the Harbor registry cache; and publishes the `dev` tag without image scanning or signing. The current `dev` image is kept as `previous` before replacement. Knowledge-Core/deploy is the editable deploy source; CI copies it to the Knowledge-Core/deploy snapshot in HappyLadySauceM/deploy, updates root image digests, and pushes with a fast-forward compare-and-swap check and bounded retry. Deploy-only changes skip image builds but run deployment validation, GitOps synchronization, Argo health, and dev smoke before promoting `dev` to `main`; code changes run the complete image chain. If Argo or smoke fails, CI restores the exact GitOps snapshot commit with an ordinary fast-forward and moves each affected Harbor `previous` tag back to `dev`; rollback refuses to overwrite if the remote branch moved. After success, `previous` tags must be deleted for Harbor GC; cleanup failure blocks release. DeepSeek release summary failure blocks promotion to `main`. On success, `dev` fast-forwards to `main` and creates one aggregate `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` Git tag and GitHub Release, both pointing at the exact promotion commit SHA; the Release title matches the version tag. Existing knowledge-core-v* tags still count when choosing the next patch or retrying a prefixed tagged commit. Retrying the same commit reuses the matching aggregate tag and existing Release, but rejects a tag that points at another commit. Shared history is never force-pushed or rebased.

<!-- fact:cicd.pipeline status:verified sources:.github/workflows/pipeline.yml, filesystem:ci-config, user-confirmed, user-confirmed-cicd-ratio-and-source-deploy-sync, user-confirmed-en-locale-source, user-confirmed-runner-migration -->

Run `make ci` after every change; it covers check and generate-check, including Go and Rust format checks, vet/clippy, lint, non-cached tests, build, vulnerability/supply-chain checks, and generated-file drift. Go concurrency, goroutine, orchestration, or lifecycle work also runs `make race`. Node fixture changes run `npm ci && npm run ci` under `services/collaboration/interop`. IDL changes also regenerate, review wire/API compatibility, and run `go run ./scripts/idlguard compat-git <merge-base> idl`.
